entries.title: The origin in the compound-zeta normalization
entries.locator: arXiv:1808.06789v3, §1.2.1, equations (1.15)–(1.17), PDF/printed p.5. Versioned HTML and PDF text compared; no visual PDF or journal-version check.
entries.claim: Equation (1.16) defines the base law at every lattice point while excluding the origin from its normalizing sum.
entries.problem: For the displayed cube density and L=1 the base mass is3^d/(3^d−1)>1. Its t-fold convolution has that mass to power t, so the polynomially weighted mixture has infinite total mass.
entries.correction: FIXER recommends restoring the all-lattice denominator sum_y h(y/L), including y=0, as in the cited earlier arXiv:1204.1180v4 Appendix A (A.2). Require this finite denominator to be positive. TIOJ proves normalization of the base law and its compound mixture for alpha>0, and verifies symmetry, nondegeneracy, irreducibility and aperiodicity for the cube. DTYB retains the infinite-mass counterexample and the separately normalized punctured alternative; these are different laws. The earlier Appendix A assumes alpha not equal to two, so it does not itself certify the marginal analytic hypotheses. The clipped power-law example used in G12U–6ZYT is separate; the main theorem is not contradicted.
entries.leanImpact: Formalize the base normalization, convolution-mass identity and Tonelli mixture identity. Analytic estimates (1.6), (1.9)–(1.13) require separate verification for the chosen law, especially at alpha=2. No compiled declaration, complete repaired-kernel verification or source-author confirmation is supplied. FIXER reports agreement in a DOI-linked accepted manuscript, not the final journal typesetting; no visual-PDF or final-journal audit is claimed.

resolution.summary: FIXER restores the all-lattice normalizing denominator; TIOJ verifies the resulting probability laws.
resolution.impact: The example's base law changes. Marginal analytic estimates still need their own proof; the main theorem is not contradicted.
